{{Wireless adapter |brand=Foxconn |model=MIC-B |revision=2 |upc= |ean= |asin= |price= |est_release_date= |fcc_date=09/28/2011 |manuf_country=China |is_manuf=Yes |manuf= |manuf_model= |manuf_rev= |if=USB (non-standard connector) |if_bus_version=2.0 |vendor_id= |device_id= |subvendor_id= |subdevice_id= |fcc_id=MCLMICB2 |ic_id=2878D-MICB2 |chip1_brand=Broadcom |chip1_model=BCM43237 |flags= |ant_conn=U.FL |802dot11_protocols=an |txchains=2 |rxchains=2 |sstreams=2 |oui= |lin_driver= |win_driver= }} *This device is a 5GHz wireless module used in the ''Nintendo'' Wii U. This module handles the Wi-Fi Direct connections to the Wii U gamepads :(which use [[wikipedia:Miracast|Miracast]]). It is visible [http://www.ifixit.com/Teardown/Nintendo+Wii+U+Teardown/11796/2 in '''iFixit''''s teardown].
There is a ''Macronix'' MX25L4006EZNI-12G (512KB Serial Flash) on-board.
